summary: Valerie Hansen is a historian and sinologist. She studied at Harvard University (~1975–1979) and under Victor H. Mair at the University of Pennsylvania (~1981–1987), later serving as an associate professor (~1993–1998) and Professor of History (~1998) at Yale University.
Valerie J. Roebuck is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She held posts attested in 2002 and 2013 at the University of Manchester.

Valerie Stoker is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who holds a post at Wright State University. She studied under traditional teachers D. Prahladachar and Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi.

Valery Evgenyevich Krasnodembsky was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Leningrad Oriental Institute (~1926–1930). He later worked there (1932–1942), taught at Saint Petersburg State University (1934–1942), and served as a researcher at the Institute of Ethnography (1933–1937).
Vamana was a scholar in the field of Indology who studied under traditional teachers Keshava, Dattatreya Sastri Nigudkar, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanatha.
Vamanshastri Kinjawadekar was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under traditional teachers Dattatreya, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanatha.

Van Austin Harvey was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at Occidental College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Yale University, he taught at Princeton, Southern Methodist University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Stanford University (~1978–1996).
Vandita Srivastava is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Banaras Hindu University, earning a Bachelor of Arts (Hons.) from 2004 to 2007 and a Ph.D. from 2010 to 2016.
Vanessa R. Sasson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who held an attested post at Marianopolis College in 2012 and 2022.

Vans Kennedy was an Indologist and linguist who served as judge-advocate-general in the Bombay Army (1817–1835). He was also an active member (1817) and President (1831–1835) of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Vasant Shinde is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts as Professor (attested 2006) and Professor of South Asian Archaeology (attested 2026) at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Vasile Burlă was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1866–1870) and the University of Graz (~1870–1872). He served as a university lecturer in Classics at Alexandru Ioan Cuza University (~1872–1901).

Vasilij Alekseevič Bogorodickij was a linguist who studied under Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay at Kazan State University (~1876–1880). He held docent and professorial posts at Kazan State University from 1881 to 1893 and taught at Kazan State Pedagogical University (1922–1925).

Vasilij Alekseevič Bogoslovskij was a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Moscow State University (~1949–1954), worked as a naučnyj sotrudnik at the University of Chicago (1957–1967), and joined the Institute of China and Contemporary Asia in 1968.

Vasilij Ivanovič Smirnov was an Indologist who studied at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies and under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov at Saint Petersburg State University until 1932. He served as a Docent at the Leningrad Oriental Institute (1936–1937).

Vasilij Matveevič Beskrovnyj was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov at Leningrad Oriental Institute (1926–1930). He held posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (1932), Saint Petersburg State University (1939–1956), and Moscow State University (1964).

Vasilij Vasil'evič Brodov was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the Moscow Institute of Philosophy, Literature and History (~1934–1938). He worked at the Institute of Philosophy (1956–1960), taught at Moscow State University (1962–1966), and chaired philosophy at the All-Union Correspondence Civil Engineering Institute (1966).

Vasily Mikhaylovich Alekseyev was a Sinologist who studied at Saint Petersburg University (~1898–1902) and under Édouard Chavannes (~1906–1909). He held long-term posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1910–1951) and the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1918–1951).

Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied under Franz von Erdmann, Józef Szczepan Kowalewski, and Archimandrite Daniil at Kazan State University. He became a professor at Kazan (1851) and Saint Petersburg State University (1855–1893).

Vasily Radlov worked in linguistics, Central Asian studies, and archaeology. Educated at Berlin under Schott, Pott, and Steinthal, and at Jena, he served as director of the Asiatic Museum (1885–1890) and the Peter the Great Museum of Anthropology and Ethnography (1894–1918).
